newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Carmakers flock to Brazil's northeast - minister.
newsitem.headline: Carmakers flock to Brazil's northeast - minister.

text.p: International carmakers from Russia, the Czech Republic and Asia have pledged to invest a total of $1.753 billion in Brazil's north and northeast, said Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles.
"I really do believe that the North and Northeast of Brazil will have a very strong presence of companies from Japan, Korea and China," Dornelles told reporters.

All the companies investing will be able to take advantage of fiscal incentives for investment in the region. They will also eventually be able to benefit from Brazil's car industry regime, which sets lower import tariffs for carmakers with Brazilian factories.
The Industry and Commerce Ministry listed the following projects:
-- Hyundai Motors of Korea will invest $286.2 million in Bahia state, with planned production of 20,000 vans a year, beginning in 1998.
-- Zam, a Russian concern, will invest $13.5 million in Acre state to produce 240 trucks a year, starting in 1998.
-- Asia Motors of Korea will invest $719 million in Bahia state to produce 60,000 pick-up trucks a year, with production starting in 1999.
-- Tatra do Brasil Ltd, a subsidiary of Czech truck maker Skoda, will invest $100 million in Bahia state to produce 2,200 specialized lorries, mainly for mining, starting in 1998.
-- U.S. car maker General Motors Corp will invest $160 million somewhere in the northeast to produce 60,000 Suzuki jeeps, going on line in 1998.
-- Troller, a national group, plans to invest $16 million in Ceara state to produce 2,200 jeeps a year starting in 1998.
-- Taquari group, a unit of Brazilian textile group Grupo Vicunha, plans jointly with Subaru of Japan to invest $150 million also in Ceara state to produce 25,000 Subaru cars beginning in 1999.
-- Brazilian group Araguaia plans to associate itself with an unnamed Chinese group to invest $8.8 million in Tocantins state, with planned annual capacity of 98 trucks, starting in 1998.

-- Inpavel Industria Paraibana de Veiculos Automotivos Ltda of Paraiba state will also link itself to an unnamed Chinese group to invest $300 million in the state to produce 30,000 vans a year, with production starting in 1998.
In addition, various motorcycle manufacturers from China, Italy, Japan and Korea have pledged to invest nearly $800 million in factories in the north, northeast and center west, the ministry said.
Annual planned production of those projects amounts to 600,000 motorcycles a year, with production due to start in 1998.
Dornelles said the Brazilian car industry regime and the fiscal incentives for the north, northeast and center west more than achieved their objectives.
"I would say I am even surprised. The enthusiasm of the companies has been great," Dornelles said.
